questions.stem: Which of the following are carpometacarpal or finger joints (not wrist joints)?
options: The interphalangeal joints
The proximal intercarpal joints
The metacarpophalangeal joints
The mid-carpal joint
The carpometacarpal joint of the thumb
questions.explanation: Wrist joints: radiocarpal, proximal intercarpal, mid-carpal, distal intercarpal. Carpometacarpal joints (thumb, II–V) and finger joints (MCP, IP) form the other two classes.

options: Is a trochoid joint
Is the distal joint of the thoracic limb
Is a synovial joint of the ellipsoid type
Is a saddle joint
Unites the carpus to the forearm
questions.explanation: The radiocarpal joint is an ellipsoid (condylar) diarthrosis; the saddle joint of the hand is the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb.

questions.stem: The antebrachial (forearm) articular surface of the radiocarpal joint:
options: Is more extensive than the carpal surface
Has a major transverse axis
Is convex
Is elliptical and concave
Is formed by the carpal surface of the radius and the radioulnar articular disc
questions.explanation: The forearm surface is concave; the carpal (radial) articular surface is convex and more extensive.

questions.stem: The carpal articular surface of the radius:
options: Has a lateral triangular part for the scaphoid
Occupies the lateral 2/3 of the antebrachial surface
Has a medial quadrilateral part for the lunate
Articulates with the triquetrum
Occupies the medial 1/3 of the antebrachial surface
questions.explanation: The radius occupies the lateral 2/3; the articular disc occupies the medial 1/3 and faces the lunate and triquetrum.

questions.stem: The radioulnar articular disc of the wrist:
options: Is a horizontal triangular ligament covered with cartilage
Attaches to the capitate
Attaches to the radial styloid process
Lies between the ulnar head and the carpus
Occupies the lateral 2/3 of the antebrachial surface
questions.explanation: The disc attaches to the ulnar notch of the radius and the ulnar styloid, between the ulnar head and lunate/triquetrum. Also false: "Occupies the lateral 2/3 of the antebrachial surface"; "Attaches to the capitate".

questions.stem: The radial articular surface of the carpus is formed by:
options: The trapezium
The scaphoid
The capitate
The pisiform
The lunate
questions.explanation: Scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum, joined by interosseous ligaments, form the convex carpal surface. The pisiform is not part of it. Also false: "The capitate"; "The trapezium".

questions.stem: The capsule of the radiocarpal joint attaches to:
options: The metacarpal bases
The tip of the radial styloid process only
The anterior and posterior edges of the articular disc
The periphery of the articular surfaces
The distal row of the carpus
questions.explanation: The capsule inserts around the articular surfaces and on the anterior and posterior edges of the articular disc.

questions.stem: Which ligament of the radiocarpal joint terminates on the lunate, triquetrum and hamate?
options: The palmar radiocarpal ligament
The palmar ulnocarpal ligament
The dorsal radiocarpal ligament
The radial collateral ligament of the carpus
The ulnar collateral ligament of the carpus
questions.explanation: Dorsal radiocarpal: lunate, triquetrum, hamate. Palmar radiocarpal: lunate, capitate. Palmar ulnocarpal: triquetrum, lunate, capitate.

questions.stem: About the collateral ligaments of the carpus:
options: The ulnar collateral ligament runs from the ulnar styloid to the pisiform and triquetrum
They are active ligaments
The ulnar collateral ligament terminates on the hamate
The radial collateral ligament runs from the radial styloid to the scaphoid
The radial collateral ligament terminates on the capitate
questions.explanation: Radial collateral → scaphoid; ulnar collateral → pisiform and triquetrum. They are passive ligaments.

questions.stem: Which ligaments of the radiocarpal joint attach to the ulnar styloid process?
options: The dorsal radiocarpal ligament
The palmar radiocarpal ligament
The palmar ulnocarpal ligament
The radial collateral ligament of the carpus
The ulnar collateral ligament of the carpus
questions.explanation: The palmar ulnocarpal ligament arises from the disc and ulnar styloid; the ulnar collateral ligament from the ulnar styloid. The palmar radiocarpal and radial collateral arise from the radial side.

questions.stem: The active ligaments of the radiocarpal joint include the tendons of:
options: The flexor carpi ulnaris
The flexor carpi radialis
The palmaris longus
The extensor carpi ulnaris
The extensors carpi radialis longus and brevis
questions.explanation: Six main muscles: flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris, palmaris longus, extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis.

questions.stem: A patient has a rounded swelling on the back of the wrist that becomes prominent in flexion and disappears in extension. This is most likely:
options: A fracture of the radial styloid
A rupture of the radial collateral ligament
A dislocation of the lunate
A synovial cyst
Carpal tunnel syndrome
questions.explanation: A synovial cyst is formed by synovial extensions insinuating between capsular and ligamentous fibres; it is prominent in flexion and disappears in extension.

questions.stem: About the movements of the radiocarpal joint:
options: Flexion has an amplitude of 35°
Abduction (radial tilt) has a larger amplitude than adduction
Extension has an amplitude of 50°
Abduction and adduction occur around a sagittal axis
Flexion and extension occur around a transverse axis
questions.explanation: Abduction (radial tilt) is 5°, less than adduction (ulnar tilt) 15°. Also false: "Flexion has an amplitude of 35°"; "Extension has an amplitude of 50°".

questions.stem: What is the amplitude of adduction (ulnar tilt) of the radiocarpal joint?
questions.explanation: Adduction (ulnar tilt) 15°, abduction (radial tilt) 5°, extension 35°, flexion 50°.

options: Is performed only around a transverse axis
Results from passing from one to another of the 4 previous movements
Is a circular summation movement drawing a cone
Is a pure rotation around a vertical axis
Is impossible at the radiocarpal joint
questions.explanation: Circumduction combines flexion, extension, abduction and adduction successively, drawing a cone.
